titulo: Disney layoffs vs. $9B buybacks: the math
caption:
Disney layoffs vs. $9B buybacks: the math

Disney layoffs vs. buybacks: in its Nov 17, 2026 shareholder letter (Form 8-K), Disney wrote "we do expect a portion to drop to the bottom line over time." Here is the number from the same year.

What a buyback is: a company spending its own cash to purchase its own shares back from the market. Disney's earnings release says it repurchased $9.0 billion of Disney shares across the full fiscal year 2026. Dividends are separate. Variety reports Disney is eliminating about 1,000 roles (Apr 14, 2026, citing a source familiar with the situation; the count is approximate).

The math: $9 billion in buybacks ÷ about 1,000 roles = about $9 million in buybacks per job cut.

Did Disney lay people off in 2026? Per Variety, about 1,000 roles in April. That is not the November results: the roles are from April 2026. The quoted sentence is about the efficiency program, which Disney says should reach about $3 billion in annual savings by fiscal 2029, not about layoffs.

Efficiency is the word. Buybacks are the number. (Our take.)

Send this to someone who has been through a round of cuts.

Synthetic voice. Sources: Disney earnings release (SEC), Nov 17, 2026; Variety, Apr 14, 2026.
